sampling_model.design: Condition on fixed supplied nuisance fits. The observed experiment consists only of three mutually independent evaluation folds with projected law \(Q_P=P^n\otimes P^n\otimes P^n\). Every median-of-means statistic uses \(b_n(\beta)=\min\{n,\lceil8\log(2/\beta)\rceil\}\) nonempty near-equal consecutive blocks; the coverage and frontier claims apply for \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\).
sampling_model.units: Each fold contains \(n\) independent superpopulation observations \(Z_i=(X_i,T_i,Y_i)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous treatment obeying \(T=g_0(X)+\eta\), with \(\eta\perp X\) and \(E_P[\eta^2]=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Known unit treatment-residual variance is the nondegeneracy normalization.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The statistical law class contains only primitive laws. The selected training-realized functions are external fixed inputs, and the upper theorem is uniform over all supplied pairs in \(\mathcal H_n(P)\). The Gaussian-coordinate converse is narrower: it applies to supplied-fit sequences for which the stated source fuzzy supports and a nonempty Gaussian two-point path transfer into the same projected class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.2 gives, on its full bounded-outcome Gaussian-treatment partially linear class, the minimax lower scale \(N^{-1/2}+a_Nb_N\{\log(1/a_N)/\log N\}^3\). Appendix D equation (56) supplies only the fuzzy nuisance-product/logarithmic term, while the Gaussian two-point model (57) and conclusion (58) separately supply the parametric term. Theorem 5.4 gives a fixed-positive-cumulant ACE point-estimation upper bound on a separate class.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The direct published-class Gaussian-coordinate inclusion theorem and Open-ended Questions 7--9

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 and Proposition 2 characterize expected-length adaptation over unions in Gaussian linear-functional experiments.
The paper obtains composite-hypothesis lower bounds by moment-matched priors and chi-square control of normal mixtures.
Theorem 5 rules out second-order partially linear model orthogonality under Gaussian residuals, while Theorems 8--10 construct higher-order moments under non-Gaussian residuals.
Theorem 2 establishes coverage and interval-length control for the filtered union, while Theorem 3 supplies the oracle-proximity and existence ingredient.

body.tldr: For a primitive JMS partially linear law and fixed training-realized nuisance fits supplied within stated \(L^8(P_X)\) radii, one interval is honest over exact-Gaussian and shrinking fourth-cumulant-separated branches of the projected evaluation experiment. Four explicit Bonferroni-calibrated median-of-means events use nonempty finite-sample block partitions and cover safe DML, four residual moments, centered Appell inversion, and its empirical slope. The non-Gaussian finite-sample length is \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n+d_np_{\mathrm{sel},n}\}\), with an explicit bound on \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\), and reduces to \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n\}\) when \(\delta_n/s_n\to\infty\). For bounded supplied-fit sequences satisfying the published pointwise fit bounds and nuisance-product condition, direct inclusion of the full Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis Gaussian class yields the certified Gaussian coordinate \(d_n^-=n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\); it needs neither conditional-transfer axioms nor an auxiliary outcome-variance subclass. A common-fit branch selector rules out the bounded-chi-square cross-branch fuzzy route at strong separation. The logarithm in \(\Lambda_n\), the within-non-Gaussian lower face, and hence a matching Pareto frontier remain open, and no improvement of global union-supremum expected length is claimed.

project_justification.gap: Published structure-agnostic partially linear model theory and the sibling repository paper study separate Gaussian or fixed-non-Gaussian point-estimation classes and fixed-separation spectral constructions, not one conditionally specified projected experiment with union honesty, shrinking cumulant separation, and branchwise expected length. Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis do supply the exact full-class Gaussian minimax benchmark, including its retained logarithmic factor, but not the local-to-Gaussian union-honest frontier.
project_justification.niche: The informative object is the two-coordinate expected-length region. The global union supremum remains governed by the Gaussian coordinate, while fixed positive-weight scalarizations are rate-degenerate and do not encode branchwise adaptation.
project_justification.fill: The proved upper component combines explicit nonempty-block four-event calibration, a finite-sample branch-selection error envelope, a safe unnormalized DML interval, and a fully centered split Appell inversion. On bounded supplied-fit sequences obeying the source bounds and product condition, a direct inclusion of the full Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis class into the present Gaussian branch, followed by the interval-length reduction, proves \(L_G(C_n)\gtrsim n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\). This transfer fixes interior constants inside the present envelope and uses upward closure from the included subclass; it does not assume support-by-support transfer, conditional outcome-variance nondegeneracy, or a fit-dependent oracle family. The selector impossibility theorem closes the bounded-chi-square cross-branch fuzzy route at strong separation, while the within-non-Gaussian lower face and removal of \(\Lambda_n\) remain open.

body.related_work: Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis, Theorem 3.2, give the full-class Gaussian-treatment minimax lower scale \(N^{-1/2}+a_Nb_N\{\log(1/a_N)/\log N\}^3\) for bounded supplied fits. Their Appendix D equation (56) derives only the nuisance-product/logarithmic term from moment-matched fuzzy hypotheses; their Gaussian model (57) and conclusion (58) separately derive the parametric term. The present Gaussian-coordinate theorem transfers that published theorem by direct inclusion of an interior fixed-constant subclass, rather than by postulating compatibility of particular fuzzy supports. Their Theorem 5.4 informs the fixed-separation ACE component but does not give a union-honest shrinking-cumulant interval. Mackey, Syrgkanis, and Zadik, Theorems 5 and 8--10, inform the Gaussian obstruction and higher-order score. Cai and Low, Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, inform branchwise expected length, while their Gaussian model has no learned partially linear residual; their 2011 Hermite mixture method informs the fuzzy-prior handle. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman inform localized product-mixture calculations. Chernozhukov et al. supply the split DML benchmark. Zheng, Bonvini, and Guo's Theorem 2 informs filtered-union coverage and interval-length control, while their Theorem 3 supplies the oracle-proximity and existence ingredient; neither theorem uses treatment cumulants. The sibling repository paper \(\texttt{stat\_sa\_plm\_cumulant\_converse}\) proves fixed-separation spectral and estimation constructions and explicitly leaves shrinking separation, adaptive switching, uniform inference, and a local matching lower bound unresolved. The present proved contribution is the conditional supplied-fit shrinking-separation upper frontier together with the direct-inclusion Gaussian coordinate at \(d_n^-\); it does not claim a matching Pareto frontier. Quessy and Mailhot analyze centered and studentized normality statistics without nuisance-contaminated residuals. Armstrong, Kline, and Sun motivate caution about pretesting for a different point-risk object.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The certified Gaussian lower coordinate is \(d_n^-=n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_{g,n}\varepsilon_{q,n}\Lambda_n\), not \(d_n\) in regimes where \(\Lambda_n\) vanishes. Its direct published-class inclusion applies to bounded supplied-fit sequences satisfying the source pointwise bounds and product smallness condition, after fixing interior constants compatible with the stated universal lower threshold on \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\); it does not cover arbitrary unbounded external fits. The source's full minimax theorem combines two different mechanisms: equation (56) gives only the fuzzy nuisance-product/logarithmic term, and equations (57)--(58) give the separate parametric term. The upper theorem does not need the lower-subclass fit bounds and does not identify a matching Pareto boundary. Its finite-sample guarantee starts at \(n=\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), when every requested calibration block count is available. The early bounded-chi-square cross-branch Rademacher/Hermite route is resolved negatively at strong separation because the common-fit selector makes the mixtures asymptotically singular; a within-non-Gaussian or constrained-risk experiment is still required for the actual lower frontier.
body.honest_scope: The law class is primitive and contains no learner-performance condition. All upper-frontier inference is conditional on fixed supplied fits and uniform over their radius set. The Appell polynomial estimates the first four raw residual moments on a fold independent of inversion. Every median-of-means operator partitions the sample into \(b_n(\beta)=\min\{n,\lceil8\log(2/\beta)\rceil\}\) nonempty blocks, and the upper theorem assumes \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\). Four named events receive error \(\alpha/4\) each, while the separate bound \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\) quantifies wrong-branch selection. The Gaussian lower theorem takes \(N=3n\), fixes source constants strictly inside the present envelope once \(C_{\mathrm{env}}\) exceeds the stated universal feasibility threshold, and includes the full \(s=8\), \(\sigma=1\) Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis class for every bounded supplied-fit sequence satisfying their pointwise fit bounds and nuisance-product condition. Constant conditional \(\mathcal N(0,1)\) treatment noise is independent of \(X\) and has unit variance; the source partially linear laws impose \(E[\xi\mid X,T]=0\); and bounded \(Y\), \(q_0\), \(\theta_0\), and \(g_0\), together with Gaussian \(\eta\), give the required unconditional sub-Gaussian envelope after the fixed constants are chosen. The source \(L^8\) balls are exactly the present supplied-fit set, so upward transfer and the interval-length reduction yield the Gaussian coordinate. No support-localization axiom, auxiliary conditional outcome-variance condition, or nondegenerate Gaussian subclass is used. The sibling repository paper settles fixed-separation spectral estimation, not this local-to-Gaussian union-honest length problem. The within-non-Gaussian converse and removal of \(\Lambda_n\) are open. No matching Pareto boundary or improvement of global union-supremum expected length is claimed.
